cards.b: Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions as work progresses.
First-hand: your own drawings, photographs, visits and observations.
Made by someone else: books, magazines, websites, other artists' work; cite it.
What you are trying to explore or say; show them clearly in your work.
Drawing an outline while looking only at the subject, not the paper.
Drawing without lifting the pencil, for flow and confidence.
A small quick sketch to try out a composition.
The relative size of parts of a subject; check by measuring with a pencil.
Draw the gaps between parts to correct shapes and proportions.
Use a paper frame to select a section for a more interesting composition.
Where you look from; try high, low, close or partial views.
Drawings, photographs, notes, mind maps, swatches and visits: higher AO1 bands need variety.
Keep adding observations through the project, not only at the start.
A page of small photographs of one subject; select the best and say why.
Names the subject, medium, technique, a decision and an intention.

gaps.s: A drawing made from real life is called an ___ drawing.
Your own drawings and photographs are ___ sources.
Images from books or websites are ___ sources.
A small quick layout sketch is called a ___.
The relative size of parts of a subject is its ___.
What you aim to say or achieve in your work is your ___.
Drawing the gaps between objects means drawing the ___ space.
A top AO1 mark needs recording from a ___ of relevant sources.

short.q: Why should you include first-hand studies?
short.model: They show your own looking and drawing skill and give variety of sources, which AO1's higher bands require.

short.q: Suggest three ways to record a theme of 'Streets'.
short.model: Draw buildings on location, take photographs from several viewpoints, and make notes or sketch at a gallery or from an interview with someone local.

short.q: How do you show intentions as work progresses?
short.model: Write short aims, choose sources that fit them, and review and adjust the plan with comments.

short.q: Describe how to check proportions in a drawing.
short.model: Hold a pencil at arm's length to measure one part and compare it with others, and check angles and negative spaces.

short.q: Why can photographs alone limit AO1?
short.model: They show little drawing skill and may look less personal, so skill in recording is not fully shown.
